subject: physics
title: Astrophysics Adventure 1: Stellar properties — luminosity and magnitude
welcome_lead: Today you'll measure stars — luminosity, magnitude, parallax.
meta_desc: IBDP Physics — luminosity, apparent vs absolute magnitude, parsec, parallax.
final_note: You learned L = σA T⁴ for stars, parallax measures distance (1 pc = 3.26 ly), m - M = 5 log(d/10) links apparent and absolute magnitudes.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Star as blackbody: L = σ · 4πR² · T⁴.

Sun L_⊙ = 3.85 × 10²⁶ W.

Apparent brightness (flux) at Earth: b = L / (4πd²).

So measuring b and knowing L gives distance.

Logarithmic, smaller = brighter. Originally Hipparchus' eyes.

5 magnitudes = factor 100 in brightness. So 1 magnitude ≈ 2.512×.

Apparent m: as seen from Earth.
Absolute M: if star at 10 pc.

Distance modulus: m − M = 5 log(d/10) (d in pc).

Earth orbits → nearby stars shift against distant ones over 6 months.

Parallax angle p (arcsec): d (pc) = 1/p (arcsec).

1 pc = distance where parallax is 1 arcsec = 3.26 ly = 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m.

Limited to ~kpc for ground-based; Gaia satellite to ~50 kpc.
